entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline for verifying LLM-generated mathematical solutions using 3 AI agents, combining automatic and interactive verification with proof assistants as an alternative to answer-only checking.

entry.title: Multimodal Crystal Flow: Any-to-Any Modality Generation for Unified Crystal Modeling

author.name: Kiyoung Seong, Sungsoo Ahn, Sehui Han, Changyoung Park

entry.summary: Proposes MCFlow, a unified multimodal flow model for crystal generation that handles multiple tasks (crystal structure prediction, de novo generation) via independent time variables in a standard transformer.

entry.title: CodeHacker: Automated Test Case Generation for Detecting Vulnerabilities in Competitive Programming Solutions

author.name: Jingwei Shi, Xinxiang Yin, Jing Huang, Jinman Zhao, Shengyu Tao

entry.summary: Proposes CodeHacker, an automated agent for generating adversarial test cases to expose vulnerabilities in code submissions, using stress testing, anti-hash attacks, and logic-specific targeting strategies.

entry.title: Right to History: A Sovereignty Kernel for Verifiable AI Agent Execution

author.name: Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes 'Right to History' - the principle that individuals deserve verifiable records of AI agent actions on their hardware. Formalizes via five system invariants inspired by Floridi's informational rights framework.

entry.title: Case-Aware LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation for Enterprise-Scale RAG Systems

author.name: Mukul Chhabra, Luigi Medrano, Arush Verma

entry.summary: Presents a case-aware LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation framework for enterprise multi-turn RAG systems with eight operationally grounded metrics that separate retrieval quality from generation quality across turns.

entry.title: RMIT-ADM+S at the MMU-RAG NeurIPS 2025 Competition

author.name: Kun Ran, Marwah Alaofi, Danula Hettiachchi, Chenglong Ma, Khoi Nguyen Dinh Anh, Khoi Vo Nguyen, Sachin Pathiyan Cherumanal, Lida Rashidi, Falk Scholer, Damiano Spina, Shuoqi Sun, Oleg Zendel

entry.summary: Presents R2RAG, an award-winning RAG system from RMIT for the NeurIPS 2025 MMU-RAG competition that dynamically adapts retrieval strategy based on query complexity, operating on a single consumer GPU.

entry.title: Toward an Agentic Infused Software Ecosystem

author.name: Mark Marron

entry.summary: Outlines a vision for an Agentic Infused Software Ecosystem (AISE) built on three pillars: AI agents, programming languages/APIs as communication substrate, and runtime environments.

entry.title: Quantitative Approximation Rates for Group Equivariant Learning

author.name: Jonathan W. Siegel, Snir Hordan, Hannah Lawrence, Ali Syed, Nadav Dym

entry.summary: Provides quantitative approximation rates for group equivariant neural networks on Hölder functions, bridging the gap between universal approximation properties and concrete rate guarantees for equivariant models.

entry.title: Sample-efficient evidence estimation of score based priors for model selection

author.name: Frederic Wang, Katherine L. Bouman

entry.summary: Proposes a sample-efficient method for estimating model evidence with diffusion priors for Bayesian model selection in imaging inverse problems, avoiding the need for many evaluations of the prior density.

entry.title: Fuz-RL: A Fuzzy-Guided Robust Framework for Safe Reinforcement Learning under Uncertainty

author.name: Xu Wan, Chao Yang, Cheng Yang, Jie Song, Mingyang Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Fuz-RL, a fuzzy measure-guided framework for safe reinforcement learning that uses Choquet integrals for robust value estimation, proving equivalence to distributionally robust safe RL.

entry.title: Knowing the Unknown: Interpretable Open-World Object Detection via Concept Decomposition Model

author.name: Xueqiang Lv, Shizhou Zhang, Yinghui Xing, Di Xu, Peng Wang, Yanning Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces IPOW, an interpretable open-world object detection framework using concept decomposition to explicitly separate discriminative, shared, and background features. Aims to address the known-unknown confusion problem in open-world detection.

entry.title: Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs

author.name: Junyu Bi, Xinting Niu, Daixuan Cheng, Kun Yuan, Tao Wang, Binbin Cao, Jian Wu, Yuning Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes using LLMs for generative pseudo-labeling in recommendation system pre-ranking to address train-serving discrepancy and sample selection bias, particularly for unexposed and long-tail content.

entry.title: An Expert Schema for Evaluating Large Language Model Errors in Scholarly Question-Answering Systems

author.name: Anna Martin-Boyle, William Humphreys, Martha Brown, Cara Leckey, Harmanpreet Kaur

entry.summary: Develops a validated error schema for evaluating LLM errors in scholarly QA systems, identifying 20 error patterns across seven categories through collaboration with domain experts and contextual inquiries.

entry.title: CLIPoint3D: Language-Grounded Few-Shot Unsupervised 3D Point Cloud Domain Adaptation

author.name: Mainak Singha, Sarthak Mehrotra, Paolo Casari, Subhasis Chaudhuri, Elisa Ricci, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: Introduces CLIPoint3D, the first framework for few-shot unsupervised 3D point cloud domain adaptation built on CLIP, using depth map projections and knowledge-driven prompt tuning to handle synthetic-to-real domain shifts.

entry.title: Efficient and Explainable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Masked Vision-Language-Action Diffusion

author.name: Jiaru Zhang, Manav Gagvani, Can Cui, Juntong Peng, Ruqi Zhang, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: Proposes MVLAD-AD, combining vision-language understanding with diffusion-based planning for autonomous driving. Uses masked tokens to bridge efficient planning with semantic explainability.

entry.title: AnimeAgent: Is the Multi-Agent via Image-to-Video models a Good Disney Storytelling Artist?

author.name: Hailong Yan, Shice Liu, Tao Wang, Xiangtao Zhang, Yijie Zhong, Jinwei Chen, Le Zhang, Bo Li

entry.summary: AnimeAgent is the first Image-to-Video multi-agent framework for custom storyboard generation, inspired by Disney's animation workflow. It addresses content consistency, dynamic expressiveness, and iterative correction limitations of static diffusion-based approaches.

entry.title: Real-time Motion Segmentation with Event-based Normal Flow

author.name: Sheng Zhong, Zhongyang Ren, Xiya Zhu, Dehao Yuan, Cornelia Fermuller, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time motion segmentation method using event-based cameras with normal flow as an intermediate representation, compressing motion information from event clusters for efficient processing in dynamic scenes.

entry.title: Le-DETR: Revisiting Real-Time Detection Transformer with Efficient Encoder Design

author.name: Jiannan Huang, Aditya Kane, Fengzhe Zhou, Yunchao Wei, Humphrey Shi

entry.summary: Le-DETR revisits real-time DETR design with EfficientNAT backbone combining efficient convolution and local attention, achieving high performance with low pre-training cost, making exploration of novel backbones more accessible.

entry.title: OCR-Agent: Agentic OCR with Capability and Memory Reflection

author.name: Shimin Wen, Zeyu Zhang, Xingdou Bian, Hongjie Zhu, Lulu He, Layi Shama, Daji Ergu, Ying Cai

entry.summary: OCR-Agent proposes an iterative self-correction framework for VLMs with Capability Reflection (error diagnosis and correction planning) and Memory Reflection (leveraging past correction experience) for improved OCR performance.

entry.title: FACTO: Function-space Adaptive Constrained Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Yichang Feng, Xiao Liang, Minghui Zheng

entry.summary: FACTO introduces function-space trajectory optimization for robotic manipulators, parameterizing trajectories as linear combinations of orthogonal basis functions and optimizing in coefficient space with adaptive constrained updates.

entry.title: Bioanchors 2: Electric Bacilli

author.name: TsviBT

entry.summary: Critiques arguments for fast AGI timelines, arguing that while progress indicators (scaling, investment, researcher pivoting) are valid, they don't provide enough information about absolute proximity to AGI without knowing 'how much of what you need do you have.'

entry.title: Online Algorithms with Unreliable Guidance

author.name: Julien Dallot, Yuval Emek, Yuval Gil, Maciej Pacut, Stefan Schmid

entry.summary: Introduces Online Algorithms with Unreliable Guidance (OAG), a formal model for ML-augmented online decision making where guidance is adversarially corrupted with probability β. Provides consistency and robustness analysis.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Robust Mean Estimation with Untrusted Batches

author.name: Maryam Aliakbarpour, Vladimir Braverman, Yuhan Liu, Junze Yin

entry.summary: Studies high-dimensional robust mean estimation with untrusted batches under a double corruption model combining adversarial users and distributional deviation, providing new error bounds.

entry.title: On the Generalization Behavior of Deep Residual Networks From a Dynamical System Perspective

author.name: Jinshu Huang, Mingfei Sun, Chunlin Wu

entry.summary: Establishes generalization error bounds for both discrete and continuous-time ResNets using Rademacher complexity and dynamical systems flow maps, showing depth-uniform bounds of order O(1/√S).

entry.title: DANCE: Doubly Adaptive Neighborhood Conformal Estimation

author.name: Brandon R. Feng, Brian J. Reich, Daniel Beaglehole, Xihaier Luo, David Keetae Park, Shinjae Yoo, Zhechao Huang, Xueyu Mao, Olcay Boz, Jungeum Kim

entry.summary: Proposes DANCE, a conformal prediction method for classification that uses nearest-neighbor approaches in embedding space rather than logit scores. Combines two novel nonconformity scores for better uncertainty quantification with pre-trained models.

entry.title: Robust Spiking Neural Networks Against Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Shuai Wang, Malu Zhang, Yulin Jiang, Dehao Zhang, Ammar Belatreche, Yu Liang, Yimeng Shan, Zijian Zhou, Yang Yang, Haizhou Li

entry.summary: Proposes Threshold Guarding Optimization (TGO) for improving adversarial robustness of spiking neural networks, theoretically identifying threshold-neighboring neurons as the key vulnerability factor.

entry.title: BoxSplitGen: A Generative Model for 3D Part Bounding Boxes in Varying Granularity

author.name: Juil Koo, Wei-Tung Lin, Chanho Park, Chanhyeok Park, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: BoxSplitGen generates 3D part bounding boxes at varying granularity through iterative splitting, enabling intuitive coarse-to-fine 3D shape generation. The framework supports interactive 3D creation by progressively refining abstract shapes into detailed structures.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Cross-Modality Medical Image Segmentation via Augmentation-Driven Generalization

author.name: Sachin Dudda Nagaraju, Ashkan Moradi, Bendik Skarre Abrahamsen, Mattijs Elschot

entry.summary: Addresses cross-modality domain shifts in federated learning for medical image segmentation, where each client holds only CT or MRI data. Uses augmentation-driven generalization without requiring paired multimodal data.

entry.title: MUSE: Harnessing Precise and Diverse Semantics for Few-Shot Whole Slide Image Classification

author.name: Jiahao Xu, Sheng Huang, Xin Zhang, Zhixiong Nan, Jiajun Dong, Nankun Mu

entry.summary: MUSE proposes stochastic multi-view semantic enhancement for few-shot whole slide image classification, refining class-level semantic priors into sample-wise adapted representations via retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Dropping Anchor and Spherical Harmonics for Sparse-view Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Shuangkang Fang, I-Chao Shen, Xuanyang Zhang, Zesheng Wang, Yufeng Wang, Wenrui Ding, Gang Yu, Takeo Igarashi

entry.summary: DropAnSH-GS proposes anchor-based dropout for sparse-view Gaussian Splatting that removes spatial neighbor groups instead of individual Gaussians, and also addresses overfitting from high-degree spherical harmonics.

entry.title: OmniOCR: Generalist OCR for Ethnic Minority Languages

author.name: Bonan Liu, Zeyu Zhang, Bingbing Meng, Han Wang, Hanshuo Zhang, Chengping Wang, Daji Ergu, Ying Cai

entry.summary: OmniOCR presents a universal OCR framework for ethnic minority scripts using Dynamic LoRA to allocate model capacity across layers and scripts, with sparsity regularization for efficient adaptation while preserving knowledge.

entry.title: Vision-Based Reasoning with Topology-Encoded Graphs for Anatomical Path Disambiguation in Robot-Assisted Endovascular Navigation

author.name: Jiyuan Zhao, Zhengyu Shi, Wentong Tian, Tianliang Yao, Dong Liu, Tao Liu, Yizhe Wu, Peng Qi

entry.summary: SCAR-UNet-GAT is a two-stage framework for robotic path planning in coronary intervention, using attention-regularized U-Net for vessel segmentation and graph attention networks for topology-encoded path disambiguation.

entry.title: KCFRC: Kinematic Collision-Aware Foothold Reachability Criteria for Legged Locomotion

author.name: Lei Ye, Haibo Gao, Huaiguang Yang, Peng Xu, Haoyu Wang, Tie Liu, Junqi Shan, Zongquan Deng, Liang Ding

entry.summary: KCFRC introduces kinematic collision-aware foothold reachability analysis for legged robots, establishing sufficient conditions and an efficient algorithm for validating non-collision swing trajectories in real-time.

entry.title: GauS: Differentiable Scheduling Optimization via Gaussian Reparameterization

author.name: Yaohui Cai, Vesal Bakhtazad, Cunxi Yu, Zhiru Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes GauS, a differentiable scheduling framework using Gaussian reparameterization that models operator scheduling as continuous variables, reducing parameter space and leveraging GPU parallelism.

entry.title: Exploring the Impact of Parameter Update Magnitude on Forgetting and Generalization of Continual Learning

author.name: JinLi He, Liang Bai, Xian Yang

entry.summary: Characterizes forgetting in continual learning from the parameter update magnitude perspective, deriving optimal update magnitudes that minimize forgetting and unifying frozen and initialized training paradigms.

entry.title: Leveraging Causal Reasoning Method for Explaining Medical Image Segmentation Models

author.name: Limai Jiang, Ruitao Xie, Bokai Yang, Huazhen Huang, Juan He, Yufu Huo, Zikai Wang, Yang Wei, Yunpeng Cai

entry.summary: Introduces a causal inference-based explanation method for medical image segmentation, using average treatment effect (ATE) backpropagation to determine influence of input regions and network components on segmentation outputs.

entry.title: Long-Term Multi-Session 3D Reconstruction Under Substantial Appearance Change

author.name: Beverley Gorry, Tobias Fischer, Michael Milford, Alejandro Fontan

entry.summary: Addresses long-term multi-session 3D reconstruction under substantial appearance change (e.g., coral reef monitoring) by enforcing cross-session correspondences within joint SfM rather than post-hoc alignment.

entry.title: CleanStyle: Plug-and-Play Style Conditioning Purification for Text-to-Image Stylization

author.name: Xiaoman Feng, Mingkun Lei, Yang Wang, Dingwen Fu, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: CleanStyle is a plug-and-play framework that removes content leakage from style embeddings in diffusion-based style transfer using SVD decomposition. It identifies that content leakage stems from tail components of style embeddings.

entry.title: Cycle-Consistent Tuning for Layered Image Decomposition

author.name: Zheng Gu, Min Lu, Zhida Sun, Dani Lischinski, Daniel Cohen-O, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Presents a cycle-consistent tuning framework for layered image decomposition using diffusion models, focusing on logo-object decomposition with jointly trained decomposition and composition models.

entry.title: Seeing Through Words: Controlling Visual Retrieval Quality with Language Models

author.name: Jianglin Lu, Simon Jenni, Kushal Kafle, Jing Shi, Handong Zhao, Yun Fu

entry.summary: Proposes quality-controllable text-to-image retrieval that uses language models to expand short, ambiguous queries with contextual details and explicit image quality specifications.

entry.title: LST-SLAM: A Stereo Thermal SLAM System for Kilometer-Scale Dynamic Environments

author.name: Zeyu Jiang, Kuan Xu, Changhao Chen

entry.summary: LST-SLAM is a stereo thermal SLAM system for kilometer-scale dynamic environments, combining self-supervised thermal feature learning with semantic-geometric constraints to suppress dynamic objects.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Learning with Online Expert Correction for Autonomous Catheter Steering in Endovascular Bifurcation Navigation

author.name: Hao Wang, Tianliang Yao, Bo Lu, Zhiqiang Pei, Liu Dong, Lei Ma, Peng Qi

entry.summary: Proposes a sample-efficient RL framework with online expert correction for autonomous catheter steering in endovascular navigation, integrating segmentation-based pose estimation with expert-guided exploration.

entry.title: Acoustic Feedback for Closed-Loop Force Control in Robotic Grinding

author.name: Zongyuan Zhang, Christopher Lehnert, Will N. Browne, Jonathan M. Roberts

entry.summary: AFRG uses a contact microphone to estimate grinding force from audio signals for closed-loop force control in robotic grinding, replacing expensive force sensors with low-cost acoustic feedback.

entry.title: Balancing Multiple Objectives in Urban Traffic Control with Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback

author.name: Chenyang Zhao, Vinny Cahill, Ivana Dusparic

entry.summary: Applies RLAIF (RL from AI feedback) to multi-objective urban traffic control, using LLMs to generate preference labels for balancing conflicting objectives like throughput and emissions.

entry.title: OpenPort Protocol: A Security Governance Specification for AI Agent Tool Access

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang, Ziyuan Wang, Zhida Li, Qiang Li

entry.summary: Introduces OpenPort Protocol (OPP), a governance-first specification for secure AI agent tool access, covering authorization, audit logging, and abuse resistance in a model-neutral framework.

entry.title: MultiModalPFN: Extending Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Multimodal Tabular Learning

author.name: Wall Kim, Chaeyoung Song, Hanul Kim

entry.summary: Extends TabPFN to handle multimodal tabular data (images, text) through MMPFN with modality projectors including multi-head gated MLP and cross-attention pooler.

entry.title: Hierarchical Molecular Representation Learning via Fragment-Based Self-Supervised Embedding Prediction

author.name: Jiele Wu, Haozhe Ma, Zhihan Guo, Thanh Vinh Vo, Tze Yun Leong

entry.summary: Proposes GraSPNet, a hierarchical self-supervised framework for molecular graph learning that explicitly models both atomic-level and fragment-level semantics by decomposing molecules into chemically meaningful fragments.

entry.title: TrajGPT-R: Generating Urban Mobility Trajectory with Reinforcement Learning-Enhanced Generative Pre-trained Transformer

author.name: Jiawei Wang, Chuang Yang, Jiawei Yong, Xiaohang Xu, Hongjun Wang, Noboru Koshizuka, Shintaro Fukushima, Ryosuke Shibasaki, Renhe Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces TrajGPT-R, a transformer-based framework for generating urban mobility trajectories using offline reinforcement learning and inverse RL to capture trajectory-level reward signals.

entry.title: Multimodal MRI Report Findings Supervised Brain Lesion Segmentation with Substructures

author.name: Yubin Ge, Yongsong Huang, Xiaofeng Liu

entry.summary: Proposes report-supervised brain lesion segmentation that handles multi-parametric MRI with hierarchical report findings, addressing challenges of qualitative/uncertain cues and partial annotations.

entry.title: Tensor Network Generator-Enhanced Optimization for Traveling Salesman Problem

author.name: Ryo Sakai, Chen-Yu Liu

entry.summary: Applies tensor network generator-enhanced optimization (TN-GEO) with matrix product states to the traveling salesman problem, using permutation-based formulation with autoregressive sampling to guarantee valid tours.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion with Sample-Efficient Estimators for Conditionals

author.name: Karthik Elamvazhuthi, Abhijith Jayakumar, Andrey Y. Lokhov

entry.summary: Proposes a discrete diffusion framework using Neural Interaction Screening Estimator (NeurISE) for sample-efficient estimation of single-site conditionals, treating them as fundamental objects rather than approximating score functions. Tested on Ising models, MNIST, and quantum annealer data.

entry.title: $\kappa$-Explorer: A Unified Framework for Active Model Estimation in MDPs

author.name: Xihe Gu, Urbashi Mitra, Tara Javidi

entry.summary: Introduces κ-Explorer, a parameterized family of objective functions for active model estimation in tabular MDPs that unifies average-case and worst-case exploration objectives through a curvature parameter.

entry.title: SMaRT: Online Reusable Resource Assignment and an Application to Mediation in the Kenyan Judiciary

author.name: Shafkat Farabi, Didac Marti Pinto, Wei Lu, Manuel Ramos-Maqueda, Sanmay Das, Antoine Deeb, Anja Sautmann

entry.summary: Introduces SMaRT for online reusable resource allocation applied to mediator assignment in the Kenyan judiciary, handling 2000+ mediators and 87 geographic locations with quality learning and capacity constraints.

entry.title: PhyGHT: Physics-Guided HyperGraph Transformer for Signal Purification at the HL-LHC

author.name: Mohammed Rakib, Luke Vaughan, Shivang Patel, Flera Rizatdinova, Alexander Khanov, Atriya Sen

entry.summary: Introduces PhyGHT, a physics-guided hypergraph transformer for signal purification at the HL-LHC, combining local graph attention with global self-attention to handle ~200 simultaneous pileup collisions.

entry.title: GSNR: Graph Smooth Null-Space Representation for Inverse Problems

author.name: Romario Gualdr\'on-Hurtado, Roman Jacome, Rafael S. Suarez, Henry Arguello

entry.summary: Proposes GSNR, a method for inverse problems that imposes graph-smooth structure only on the null-space component of reconstructions, avoiding bias from general image priors. Uses a null-restricted graph Laplacian.

entry.title: BiRQA: Bidirectional Robust Quality Assessment for Images

author.name: Aleksandr Gushchin, Dmitriy S. Vatolin, Anastasia Antsiferova

entry.summary: Presents BiRQA, a compact full-reference image quality assessment metric using bidirectional multiscale pyramids with uncertainty-aware gating. Introduces Anchored Adversarial Training for robustness against adversarial perturbations.

entry.title: Pip-Stereo: Progressive Iterations Pruner for Iterative Optimization based Stereo Matching

author.name: Jintu Zheng, Qizhe Liu, HuangXin Xu, Zhuojie Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Pip-Stereo, a pruning-based approach for efficient iterative stereo matching that exploits spatial sparsity and temporal redundancy in disparity updates. Includes FlashGRU, a hardware-aware RNN operator for edge deployment.

entry.title: Beyond Human Performance: A Vision-Language Multi-Agent Approach for Quality Control in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing

author.name: Subhra Jyoti Mandal, Lara Rachidi, Puneet Jain, Matthieu Duvinage, Sander W. Timmer

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent VLM system for pharmaceutical colony-forming unit detection that surpasses human performance, achieving 99% detection rate. Uses Detectron2 with GPT-4o-based agentic validation.

entry.title: WildGHand: Learning Anti-Perturbation Gaussian Hand Avatars from Monocular In-the-Wild Videos

author.name: Hanhui Li, Xuan Huang, Wanquan Liu, Yuhao Cheng, Long Chen, Yiqiang Yan, Xiaodan Liang, Chenqiang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces WildGHand for 3D hand avatar reconstruction from in-the-wild monocular videos, using dynamic perturbation disentanglement to handle hand-object interactions, extreme poses, and other real-world degradations.

entry.title: An interactive enhanced driving dataset for autonomous driving

author.name: Haojie Feng, Peizhi Zhang, Mengjie Tian, Xinrui Zhang, Zhuoren Li, Junpeng Huang, Xiurong Wang, Junfan Zhu, Jianzhou Wang, Dongxiao Yin, Lu Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes the Interactive Enhanced Driving Dataset (IEDD) for autonomous driving, mining interactive scenarios from naturalistic data and constructing VQA-aligned BEV videos for training Vision-Language-Action models.

entry.title: RecoverMark: Robust Watermarking for Localization and Recovery of Manipulated Faces

author.name: Haonan An, Xiaohui Ye, Guang Hua, Yihang Tao, Hangcheng Cao, Xiangyu Yu, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: RecoverMark proposes a robust watermarking framework for detecting and recovering manipulated face regions, addressing vulnerabilities of fragile watermarks against removal attacks. It tackles the dual-watermark interference problem where robust and fragile watermarks degrade each other's effectiveness.

entry.title: Monocular Endoscopic Tissue 3D Reconstruction with Multi-Level Geometry Regularization

author.name: Yangsen Chen, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D Gaussian Splatting approach for endoscopic tissue reconstruction with multi-level geometry regularization, combining SDF-based mesh constraints with local rigidity for physically plausible deformations. Targets real-time rendering for robot-assisted surgery.

entry.title: RU4D-SLAM: Reweighting Uncertainty in Gaussian Splatting SLAM for 4D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Yangfan Zhao, Hanwei Zhang, Ke Huang, Qiufeng Wang, Zhenzhou Shao, Dengyu Wu

entry.summary: RU4D-SLAM extends Gaussian Splatting SLAM to 4D scene reconstruction in dynamic environments, introducing uncertainty reweighting to handle moving objects that complicate both reconstruction and tracking.

entry.title: Testing Effect Homogeneity and Confounding in High-Dimensional Experimental and Observational Studies

author.name: Ana Armendariz, Martin Huber

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for testing whether conditional average treatment effects are homogeneous across multiple experimental and observational studies, enabling detection of unobserved confounding by comparing CATEs between experimental and observational data.

entry.title: Adjacency Spectral Embeddings of Correlation Networks

author.name: Keith Levin

entry.summary: Provides theoretical justification for using adjacency spectral embeddings on correlation networks (where edges are pairwise correlations of time series), showing these correspond to latent space network models when time series have sparse Fourier representations.

entry.title: Motivation is Something You Need

author.name: Mehdi Acheli, Walid Gaaloul

entry.summary: Proposes a neuroscience-inspired training paradigm where a smaller model trains continuously while a larger 'motivated' model activates intermittently during notable training moments, mimicking the SEEKING emotional state.

entry.title: Mitigating "Epistemic Debt" in Generative AI-Scaffolded Novice Programming using Metacognitive Scripts

author.name: Sreecharan Sankaranarayanan

entry.summary: Proposes metacognitive scripts to mitigate 'epistemic debt' in novice programmers using LLM-assisted coding, drawing on cognitive load theory to distinguish cognitive offloading from outsourcing.

entry.title: Maximin Share Guarantees via Limited Cost-Sensitive Sharing

author.name: Hana Salavcova, Martin \v{C}ern\'y, Arpita Biswas

entry.summary: Studies fair allocation of indivisible goods with limited cost-sensitive sharing, proving that exact maximin share allocations exist when goods can be shared among at least half the agents.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 24, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment findings that challenge core assumptions about LLM trustworthiness, alongside strong theoretical work on transformer internals.

  • Can Aha Moments be Fake? finds most CoT steps are decorative rather than genuinely computational, undermining faithfulness assumptions critical for oversight.
  • A Bayesian model proves sycophantic chatbots cause delusional spiraling even in idealized rational users, establishing a formal impossibility result for naive sycophancy.
  • Agents of Chaos documents real-world failure modes of autonomous LLM agents with persistent memory, email, and shell access in a live laboratory red-team.
  • LLM stated preferences do not reliably predict downstream behavior, directly testing a precondition for strategic deception across five frontier models.

On the theoretical side, Exact Attention Sensitivity derives the operator norm of the softmax Jacobian, unifying multiple empirical observations about transformer training stability. Spilled Energy reinterprets softmax classifiers as Energy-Based Models, yielding training-free hallucination detection from output logits. IR³ reverse-engineers implicit RLHF rewards via contrastive inverse RL to interpretably detect and surgically repair reward hacking.

  • A causal study estimates Google AI Overviews reduced Wikipedia traffic by significant margins, with major web-ecosystem implications.
  • The Story is Not the Science proposes the first execution-grounded evaluation of mechanistic interpretability, finding notable discrepancies between narrative claims and actual code/data.
  • Latent Introspection reveals that Qwen 32B can detect concept injections in its own context via logit lens, with dramatic performance gaps between base and instruction-tuned models.

author.name: Natalie Shapira, Chris Wendler, Avery Yen, Gabriele Sarti, Koyena Pal, Olivia Floody, Adam Belfki, Alex Loftus, Aditya Ratan Jannali, Nikhil Prakash, Jasmine Cui, Giordano Rogers, Jannik Brinkmann, Can Rager, Amir Zur, Michael Ripa, Aruna Sankaranarayanan, David Atkinson, Rohit Gandikota, Jaden Fiotto-Kaufman, EunJeong Hwang, Hadas Orgad, P Sam Sahil, Negev Taglicht, Tomer Shabtay, Atai Ambus, Nitay Alon, Shiri Oron, Ayelet Gordon-Tapiero, Yotam Kaplan, Vered Shwartz, Tamar Rott Shaham, Christoph Riedl, Reuth Mirsky, Maarten Sap, David Manheim, Tomer Ullman, David Bau

entry.title: Can Aha Moments be Fake? Identifying True and Decorative Thinking Steps in CoT

author.name: Jiachen Zhao

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning steps in LLMs are genuinely used for computation or are merely 'decorative.' Using causal analysis, they find that the majority of CoT steps have minimal causal impact on the model's final prediction, and that 'thinking' can be steered as a linear direction in latent space, suggesting models often perform reasoning rather than actually doing it.

entry.title: Celo2: Towards Learned Optimization Free Lunch

author.name: Abhinav Moudgil, Boris Knyazev, Eugene Belilovsky

entry.summary: Celo2 shows that a simple normalized learned optimizer architecture with augmented meta-training can match or exceed VeLO (which used 4000 TPU months) using only 4.5 GPU hours, achieving practical meta-generalization.

entry.title: A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite

author.name: Maijunxian Wang, Ruisi Wang, Juyi Lin, Ran Ji, Thadd\"aus Wiedemer, Qingying Gao, Dezhi Luo, Yaoyao Qian, Lianyu Huang, Zelong Hong, Jiahui Ge, Qianli Ma, Hang He, Yifan Zhou, Lingzi Guo, Lantao Mei, Jiachen Li, Hanwen Xing, Tianqi Zhao, Fengyuan Yu, Weihang Xiao, Yizheng Jiao, Jianheng Hou, Danyang Zhang, Pengcheng Xu, Boyang Zhong, Zehong Zhao, Gaoyun Fang, John Kitaoka, Yile Xu, Hua Xu, Kenton Blacutt, Tin Nguyen, Siyuan Song, Haoran Sun, Shaoyue Wen, Linyang He, Runming Wang, Yanzhi Wang, Mengyue Yang, Ziqiao Ma, Rapha\"el Milli\`ere, Freda Shi, Nuno Vasconcelos, Daniel Khashabi, Alan Yuille, Yilun Du, Ziming Liu, Bo Li, Dahua Lin, Ziwei Liu, Vikash Kumar, Yijiang Li, Lei Yang, Zhongang Cai, Hokin Deng

entry.summary: Introduces the Very Big Video Reasoning (VBVR) Dataset with 200 curated reasoning tasks and over one million video clips—three orders of magnitude larger than existing datasets. Targets systematic evaluation of video reasoning capabilities including spatiotemporal structure, continuity, and causality.

entry.title: MACE-POLAR-1: A Polarisable Electrostatic Foundation Model for Molecular Chemistry

author.name: Ilyes Batatia, William J. Baldwin, Domantas Kuryla, Joseph Hart, Elliott Kasoar, Alin M. Elena, Harry Moore, Miko{\l}aj J. Gawkowski, Benjamin X. Shi, Venkat Kapil, Panagiotis Kourtis, Ioan-Bogdan Magd\u{a}u, G\'abor Cs\'anyi

entry.summary: Presents MACE-POLAR-1, an electrostatic foundation model for molecular chemistry that extends the MACE architecture with explicit long-range electrostatic interactions and polarizable iterations. Uses learnable Fukui functions for global charge equilibration, addressing a fundamental limitation of local-descriptor-based ML interatomic potentials.

entry.title: Early Evidence of Vibe-Proving with Consumer LLMs: A Case Study on Spectral Region Characterization with ChatGPT-5.2 (Thinking)

author.name: Brecht Verbeken, Brando Vagenende, Marie-Anne Guerry, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: Presents early evidence for 'vibe-proving' - using ChatGPT-5.2 (Thinking) as a mathematical research copilot to resolve a conjecture in spectral theory. Documents an iterative generate-referee-repair pipeline across seven conversation threads.

entry.title: VLANeXt: Recipes for Building Strong VLA Models

author.name: Xiao-Ming Wu, Bin Fan, Kang Liao, Jian-Jian Jiang, Runze Yang, Yihang Luo, Zhonghua Wu, Wei-Shi Zheng, Chen Change Loy

entry.summary: VLANeXt systematically examines the Vision-Language-Action model design space under a unified framework, dissecting choices along foundational components, perception essentials, and action modeling. Provides recipes for building strong VLA models starting from a simple baseline.

entry.title: DREAM: Deep Research Evaluation with Agentic Metrics

author.name: Elad Ben Avraham, Changhao Li, Ron Dorfman, Roy Ganz, Oren Nuriel, Amir Dudai, Aviad Aberdam, Noah Flynn, Elman Mansimov, Adi Kalyanpur, Ron Litman

entry.summary: Introduces DREAM, a framework for evaluating deep research agents that addresses the 'Mirage of Synthesis' where fluent reports mask factual/reasoning defects. Uses agentic evaluators with tool-use capabilities to assess temporal validity and factual correctness.

entry.title: Hiding in Plain Text: Detecting Concealed Jailbreaks via Activation Disentanglement

author.name: Amirhossein Farzam, Majid Behabahani, Mani Malek, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Guillermo Sapiro

entry.summary: Introduces a self-supervised framework for disentangling goal and framing in LLM activations to detect concealed jailbreaks. Constructs GoalFrameBench with controlled goal-framing variations and achieves detection without relying on structural artifacts.

entry.title: Learning to Remember: End-to-End Training of Memory Agents for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Kehao Zhang, Shangtong Gui, Sheng Yang, Wei Chen, Yang Feng

entry.summary: Proposes Unified Memory Agent (UMA), an end-to-end RL framework that unifies memory operations (CRUD) and QA within a single policy for long-context reasoning. Features dual memory with core summary and structured Memory Bank, plus a new Ledger-QA benchmark.

entry.title: OpenClaw AI Agents as Informal Learners at Moltbook: Characterizing an Emergent Learning Community at Scale

author.name: Eason Chen, Ce Guan, Ahmed Elshafiey, Zhonghao Zhao, Joshua Zekeri, Afeez Edeifo Shaibu, Emmanuel Osadebe Prince, Cyuan Jhen Wu

entry.summary: First empirical study of a large-scale informal learning community composed entirely of AI agents on Moltbook (2.8M registered agents). Finds extreme participation inequality, 'broadcasting inversion' patterns, and shallow engagement typical of early-stage communities.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Spectral Bounds on Attention Logits for Stable Low-Precision Training

author.name: Seyed Morteza Emadi

entry.summary: Derives rank-aware concentration inequalities for transformer attention logits, showing that when the interaction matrix has rank r << d, tail bounds are 8-28x tighter than rank-agnostic bounds. Applies this to derive geometry-aware scale factors for FP8 training.

entry.title: Value Entanglement: Conflation Between Different Kinds of Good In (Some) Large Language Models

author.name: Seong Hah Cho, Junyi Li, Anna Leshinskaya

entry.summary: Reveals 'value entanglement' in LLMs where moral, grammatical, and economic senses of 'good' are conflated in model representations, with moral valuation improperly influencing other value types. Shows this can be repaired through selective ablation.

entry.title: LLMs Can Learn to Reason Via Off-Policy RL

author.name: Daniel Ritter, Owen Oertell, Bradley Guo, Jonathan Chang, Kiant\'e Brantley, Wen Sun

entry.summary: Proposes OPAL, a novel off-policy RL algorithm for LLMs that embraces off-policyness rather than correcting for it, avoiding importance sampling modifications while achieving strong performance on reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Is Your Diffusion Sampler Actually Correct? A Sampler-Centric Evaluation of Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Luhan Tang, Longxuan Yu, Shaorong Zhang, Greg Ver Steeg

entry.summary: Introduces a sampler-centric oracle framework for evaluating discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) that isolates sampler-induced errors from denoiser errors using an exact HMM posterior. Shows that few-step dLLM samplers are not distributionally correct even with perfect denoisers.

entry.title: Limits of Convergence-Rate Control for Open-Weight Safety

author.name: Domenic Rosati, Xijie Zeng, Hong Huang, Sebastian Dionicio, Subhabrata Majumdar, Frank Rudzicz, Hassan Sajjad

entry.summary: Analyzes limits of convergence-rate control for open-weight model safety, develops SpecDef algorithm using spectral reparameterization, but proves a fundamental limit: attackers with sufficient knowledge can circumvent any such defense.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Extractor: Re-thinking HTML-to-Text Extraction for LLM Pretraining

author.name: Jeffrey Li, Josh Gardner, Doug Kang, Fangping Shi, Karanjeet Singh, Chun-Liang Li, Herumb Shandilya, David Hall, Oncel Tuzel, Percy Liang, Ludwig Schmidt, Hadi Pour Ansari, Fartash Faghri

entry.summary: Investigates whether using a single HTML-to-text extractor for LLM pretraining data is suboptimal. Shows that taking a union over different extractors increases token yield of DCLM-Baseline by up to 71% while maintaining benchmark performance, suggesting significant data is being lost.

entry.title: Position: General Alignment Has Hit a Ceiling; Edge Alignment Must Be Taken Seriously

author.name: Han Bao, Yue Huang, Xiaoda Wang, Zheyuan Zhang, Yujun Zhou, Carl Yang, Xiangliang Zhang, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that General Alignment (scalar reward compression) has hit a structural ceiling and proposing Edge Alignment that preserves multi-dimensional value structure, supports plural stakeholder representation, and handles irreducible uncertainty.

entry.title: Suppression or Deletion: A Restoration-Based Representation-Level Analysis of Machine Unlearning

author.name: Yurim Jang, Jaeung Lee, Dohyun Kim, Jaemin Jo, Simon S. Woo

entry.summary: Proposes a restoration-based analysis framework using Sparse Autoencoders to determine whether machine unlearning methods truly delete information or merely suppress it at the representation level. Uses inference-time steering to quantitatively distinguish suppression from deletion.

entry.title: Limited Reasoning Space: The cage of long-horizon reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Zhenyu Li, Guanlin Wu, Cheems Wang, Yongqiang Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes the Limited Reasoning Space hypothesis explaining why increasing compute budgets can cause test-time performance collapse in LLMs using chain-of-thought. Analyzes through non-autonomous stochastic dynamical systems, suggesting optimal compute allocation strategies.

entry.title: A Markovian View of Iterative-Feedback Loops in Image Generative Models: Neural Resonance and Model Collapse

author.name: Vibhas Kumar Vats, David J. Crandall, Samuel Goree

entry.summary: Models iterative feedback loops (where AI-generated content enters training data) as Markov Chains, identifying 'neural resonance' - convergence to low-dimensional invariant structures in latent space - as a mechanism underlying model collapse.

entry.title: Non-Interfering Weight Fields: Treating Model Parameters as a Continuously Extensible Function

author.name: Sarim Chaudhry

entry.summary: Proposes Non-Interfering Weight Fields (NIWF), a framework replacing fixed weight vectors with learned functions that generate weight configurations, providing structural guarantees against catastrophic forgetting by design.

entry.title: Many AI Analysts, One Dataset: Navigating the Agentic Data Science Multiverse

author.name: Martin Bertran, Riccardo Fogliato, Zhiwei Steven Wu

entry.summary: Shows that autonomous AI analysts built on LLMs can reproduce the structured analytic diversity seen in human many-analyst studies, where independent teams reach conflicting conclusions from the same dataset. Demonstrates this cheaply and at scale.

entry.title: The Geometry of Multi-Task Grokking: Transverse Instability, Superposition, and Weight Decay Phase Structure

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Extends geometric analysis of grokking to multi-task modular arithmetic, discovering staggered grokking order across operations, universal integrability of optimization trajectories, and weight decay acting as a bifurcation parameter. Identifies five consistent phenomena across tasks.

entry.title: RPU -- A Reasoning Processing Unit

author.name: Matthew Adiletta, Gu-Yeon Wei, David Brooks

entry.summary: Proposes the Reasoning Processing Unit (RPU), a chiplet-based hardware architecture designed for memory-bandwidth-bound LLM reasoning inference. Addresses the growing memory wall problem amplified by long-output reasoning workloads.

entry.title: SceneTok: A Compressed, Diffusable Token Space for 3D Scenes

author.name: Mohammad Asim, Christopher Wewer, Jan Eric Lenssen

entry.summary: SceneTok introduces a tokenizer that encodes multi-view scene information into a small set of permutation-invariant tokens disentangled from spatial grids, achieving 1-3 orders of magnitude compression while maintaining state-of-the-art reconstruction quality.

entry.title: How to Allocate, How to Learn? Dynamic Rollout Allocation and Advantage Modulation for Policy Optimization

author.name: Yangyi Fang, Jiaye Lin, Xiaoliang Fu, Cong Qin, Haolin Shi, Chaowen Hu, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: DynaMO proposes variance-minimizing rollout allocation (rather than uniform) and advantage modulation for RLVR training of LLMs, proving uniform allocation is suboptimal and deriving principled alternatives.

entry.title: Back to Blackwell: Closing the Loop on Intransitivity in Multi-Objective Preference Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Lujing Zhang, Keltin Grimes, Zhuohao Yu, Gokul Swamy, Zhiwei Steven Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Maximum Entropy Blackwell Winner (MaxEntBW), a game-theoretic solution concept for preference fine-tuning under intransitive (cyclic) preferences from multiple objectives, with practical algorithms derived from regret minimization.

entry.title: DSDR: Dual-Scale Diversity Regularization for Exploration in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhongwei Wan, Yun Shen, Zhihao Dou, Donghao Zhou, Yu Zhang, Xin Wang, Hui Shen, Jing Xiong, Chaofan Tao, Zixuan Zhong, Peizhou Huang, Mi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DSDR, a dual-scale diversity regularization framework for reinforcement learning with verifiers that promotes both global diversity among correct reasoning trajectories and coupling between token-level and trajectory-level diversity in LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Smoothness Adaptivity in Constant-Depth Neural Networks: Optimal Rates via Smooth Activations

author.name: Yuhao Liu, Zilin Wang, Lei Wu, Shaobo Zhang

entry.summary: Proves that constant-depth neural networks with smooth activations automatically exploit arbitrarily high orders of target function smoothness, achieving minimax-optimal approximation and estimation rates. In contrast, ReLU networks have strictly limited approximation order.

entry.title: How to Train Your Deep Research Agent? Prompt, Reward, and Policy Optimization in Search-R1

author.name: Yinuo Xu, Shuo Lu, Jianjie Cheng, Meng Wang, Qianlong Xie, Xingxing Wang, Ran He, Jian Liang

entry.summary: Conducts systematic study of RL for deep research agents along three dimensions: prompt template, reward function, and policy optimization. Reveals that Fast Thinking templates outperform Slow Thinking, and F1 rewards suffer from training collapse that can be fixed with action-level penalties.

entry.title: The persona selection model

author.name: Sam Marks

entry.summary: Describes the Persona Selection Model (PSM): LLMs learn diverse characters during pre-training, and post-training elicits a particular 'Assistant' persona. Surveys behavioral, generalization, and interpretability evidence and discusses implications for AI development.

entry.title: Asking the Right Questions: Improving Reasoning with Generated Stepping Stones

author.name: Hengyuan Hu, Tingchen Fu, Minqi Jiang, Alexander H Miller, Yoram Bachrach, Jakob Nicolaus Foerster

entry.summary: Introduces ARQ (Asking the Right Questions), a framework that uses a question generator to produce intermediate stepping stones (simplifications, alternative framings, subproblems) to improve LLM reasoning on hard tasks. Shows good stepping stones exist and improve performance.

entry.title: ZUNA: Flexible EEG Superresolution with Position-Aware Diffusion Autoencoders

author.name: Christopher Warner, Jonas Mago, JR Huml, Mohamed Osman, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: ZUNA is a 380M-parameter masked diffusion autoencoder for EEG superresolution that can infill missing channels for arbitrary electrode configurations. Trained on 208 public datasets (~2M channel-hours), it substantially outperforms spherical-spline interpolation.

entry.title: Information-Guided Noise Allocation for Efficient Diffusion Training

author.name: Gabriel Raya, Bac Nguyen, Georgios Batzolis, Yuhta Takida, Dejan Stancevic, Naoki Murata, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Yuki Mitsufuji, Luca Ambrogioni

entry.summary: InfoNoise proposes an information-theoretic approach to training noise schedule allocation for diffusion models, using conditional entropy rate as a data-dependent diagnostic. Replaces heuristic schedules with principled data-adaptive sampling.

entry.title: Global Low-Rank, Local Full-Rank: The Holographic Encoding of Learned Algorithms

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Investigates how grokking works in multi-task modular arithmetic, finding that while global structure is low-rank, local weight structure is full-rank—a 'holographic' encoding where the low-dimensional learning trajectory produces high-dimensional but structured weight configurations.

entry.title: Why Agent Caching Fails and How to Fix It: Structured Intent Canonicalization with Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Abhinaba Basu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that existing LLM caching methods (GPTCache, APC) fail dramatically on real benchmarks, identifies the root cause as optimizing for classification accuracy instead of cache key consistency, and proposes W5H2 structured intent decomposition achieving 91%+ accuracy with few-shot learning.

entry.title: Transformers for dynamical systems learn transfer operators in-context

author.name: Anthony Bao, Jeffrey Lai, William Gilpin

entry.summary: Studies in-context learning of dynamical systems in transformers, discovering that a small two-layer transformer trained on one dynamical system can forecast a different system without retraining. Finds a secondary double descent phenomenon and shows attention models approximate transfer operators.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Models Exploit Asymmetry to Solve Lookahead Planning Tasks

author.name: Itamar Trainin, Shauli Ravfogel, Omri Abend, Amir Feder

entry.summary: Investigates how discrete diffusion models exploit asymmetry in planning tasks - finding that reverse generation from goal to start is easier than forward generation. Shows dLLMs naturally leverage this asymmetry while autoregressive models cannot.

entry.title: Skill-Inject: Measuring Agent Vulnerability to Skill File Attacks

author.name: David Schmotz, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Sahar Abdelnabi, Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: Introduces SkillInject, a benchmark evaluating LLM agent susceptibility to prompt injection through skill files - a new attack surface created by agent skills features. Tests 202 injection-task pairs ranging from obvious to subtle attacks on widely-used agents.

entry.title: Benchmark Test-Time Scaling of General LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaochuan Li, Ryan Ming, Pranav Setlur, Abhijay Paladugu, Andy Tang, Hao Kang, Shuai Shao, Rong Jin, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces General AgentBench for evaluating general-purpose LLM agents across search, coding, reasoning, and tool-use. Systematically studies test-time scaling under sequential and parallel scaling strategies.

entry.title: DoAtlas-1: A Causal Compilation Paradigm for Clinical AI

author.name: Yulong Li, Jianxu Chen, Xiwei Liu, Chuanyue Suo, Rong Xia, Zhixiang Lu, Yichen Li, Xinlin Zhuang, Niranjana Arun Menon, Yutong Xie, Eran Segal, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: Proposes causal compilation - transforming medical evidence from narrative text into executable code with standardized estimand objects. DoAtlas-1 compiles 1,445 effect kernels supporting six executable causal queries for clinical AI.

entry.title: ReSyn: Autonomously Scaling Synthetic Environments for Reasoning Models

author.name: Andre He, Nathaniel Weir, Kaj Bostrom, Allen Nie, Darion Cassel, Sam Bayless, Huzefa Rangwala

entry.summary: Introduces ReSyn, a pipeline for autonomously generating diverse reasoning environments with verifiers for RLVR training. Qwen2.5-7B trained on ReSyn data achieves consistent gains in reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: ConfSpec: Efficient Step-Level Speculative Reasoning via Confidence-Gated Verification

author.name: Siran Liu, Cyril Y. He

entry.summary: ConfSpec proposes a confidence-gated cascaded verification framework for speculative reasoning in LLMs, exploiting the asymmetry between generation and verification difficulty. Small draft models verify reasoning steps within their competence range, resolving the trade-off between accuracy, speed, and resource efficiency.

entry.title: Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities

author.name: Spandan Garg, Yufan Huang

entry.summary: Debug2Fix enhances coding agents with interactive debugging capabilities, allowing them to access rich runtime information through debuggers rather than relying on static analysis or trial-and-error test-fix cycles.

entry.title: GIST: Targeted Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Coupled Optimization Geometry

author.name: Guanghui Min, Tianhao Huang, Ke Wan, Chen Chen

entry.summary: GIST addresses targeted data selection for instruction tuning by accounting for cross-parameter coupling in LoRA's optimization geometry. Shows that diagonal preconditioner assumptions break down in PEFT methods and proposes coupled optimization geometry-based selection.

entry.title: MANATEE: Inference-Time Lightweight Diffusion Based Safety Defense for LLMs

author.name: Chun Yan Ryan Kan, Tommy Tran, Vedant Yadav, Ava Cai, Kevin Zhu, Ruizhe Li, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: MANATEE is an inference-time defense against jailbreak attacks that uses diffusion-based density estimation over benign representation manifolds to project anomalous representations toward safe regions, requiring no harmful training data.

entry.title: DUET-VLM: Dual stage Unified Efficient Token reduction for VLM Training and Inference

author.name: Aditya Kumar Singh, Hitesh Kandala, Pratik Prabhanjan Brahma, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: DUET-VLM proposes a dual-stage plug-and-play token compression framework for vision-language models that first compresses vision encoder output, then progressively prunes visual tokens in the language backbone guided by text saliency. Claims aggressive compression with minimal accuracy loss.

entry.title: DeepInnovator: Triggering the Innovative Capabilities of LLMs

author.name: Tianyu Fan, Fengji Zhang, Yuxiang Zheng, Bei Chen, Xinyao Niu, Chengen Huang, Junyang Lin, Chao Huang

entry.summary: DeepInnovator proposes a training framework to enhance LLMs' ability to generate novel research ideas, using automated extraction of structured research knowledge and reinforcement learning to reward novelty and significance.

entry.title: TOPReward: Token Probabilities as Hidden Zero-Shot Rewards for Robotics

author.name: Shirui Chen, Cole Harrison, Ying-Chun Lee, Angela Jin Yang, Zhongzheng Ren, Lillian J. Ratliff, Jiafei Duan, Dieter Fox, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: TOPReward introduces a probabilistically grounded temporal value function that leverages pretrained video VLMs' token probabilities as zero-shot reward signals for robotic reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming

author.name: Ian Steenstra, Paola Pedrelli, Weiyan Shi, Stacy Marsella, Timothy W. Bickmore

entry.summary: Introduces an automated red-teaming framework for LLMs in mental health support, pairing AI therapists with simulated patients with dynamic cognitive-affective models. Large-scale evaluation (N=369 sessions) across six AI agents reveals concerning safety gaps.

entry.title: The LLMbda Calculus: AI Agents, Conversations, and Information Flow

author.name: Zac Garby, Andrew D. Gordon, David Sands

entry.summary: Introduces a formal lambda calculus for reasoning about LLM-based AI agent conversations, modeling information flow and attack surfaces from prompt injection. Provides semantic foundations for agent safety.

entry.title: AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Mert Cemri, Shubham Agrawal, Akshat Gupta, Shu Liu, Audrey Cheng, Qiuyang Mang, Ashwin Naren, Lutfi Eren Erdogan, Koushik Sen, Matei Zaharia, Alex Dimakis, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: AdaEvolve reformulates LLM-driven evolutionary code optimization as a hierarchical adaptive problem, using an 'accumulated improvement signal' to dynamically allocate compute across populations and mutation strategies. This addresses the inefficiency of static schedules in inference-time search loops where LLMs act as mutation operators.

entry.title: ISO-Bench: Can Coding Agents Optimize Real-World Inference Workloads?

author.name: Ayush Nangia, Shikhar Mishra, Aman Gokrani, Paras Chopra

entry.summary: Introduces ISO-Bench, a benchmark testing coding agents on real-world inference optimization tasks from vLLM and SGLang LLM serving frameworks. Uses 54 curated tasks from merged PRs with both execution-based and LLM-based metrics, addressing the problem that runtime metrics alone can be gamed.

entry.title: A Theory of How Pretraining Shapes Inductive Bias in Fine-Tuning

author.name: Nicolas Anguita, Francesco Locatello, Andrew M. Saxe, Marco Mondelli, Flavia Mancini, Samuel Lippl, Clementine Domine

entry.summary: Develops an analytical theory of the pretraining-fine-tuning pipeline in diagonal linear networks, deriving exact generalization error expressions. Shows different initializations place networks in qualitatively different regimes of feature reuse.

entry.title: LAD: Learning Advantage Distribution for Reasoning

author.name: Wendi Li, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Proposes LAD (Learning Advantage Distributions), replacing advantage maximization with distribution matching in RL for LLM reasoning. Formulates the objective as minimizing f-divergence between policy-induced and advantage-induced distributions.

entry.title: Capable but Unreliable: Canonical Path Deviation as a Causal Mechanism of Agent Failure in Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Wilson Y. Lee

entry.summary: Argues that many language agent failures are reliability failures caused by stochastic drift from canonical solution paths, not capability failures. Analyzes 515 model-task trajectories from the Toolathlon benchmark across 22 frontier models.

entry.title: Laplacian Multi-scale Flow Matching for Generative Modeling

author.name: Zelin Zhao, Petr Molodyk, Haotian Xue, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LapFlow, a framework that enhances flow matching for image generation by decomposing images into Laplacian pyramid residuals and processing scales in parallel via mixture-of-transformers with causal attention. Eliminates need for bridging processes between scales unlike cascaded approaches.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Control for Non-Monotonic Losses

author.name: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos

entry.summary: Extends conformal risk control to non-monotonic losses with multidimensional parameters, where guarantees depend on algorithm stability. Provides applications to selective classification, tumor segmentation, and multigroup debiasing.

entry.title: Do LLMs and VLMs Share Neurons for Inference? Evidence and Mechanisms of Cross-Modal Transfer

author.name: Chenhang Cui, An Zhang, Yuxin Chen, Gelei Deng, Jingnan Zheng, Zhenkai Liang, Xiang Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs and VLMs share neurons for inference, finding that >50% of top-activated units during multi-step inference overlap. Shows these shared neurons encode consistent and interpretable computation through causal probing.

entry.title: tttLRM: Test-Time Training for Long Context and Autoregressive 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Chen Wang, Hao Tan, Wang Yifan, Zhiqin Chen, Yuheng Liu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Sai Bi, Lingjie Liu, Yiwei Hu

entry.summary: Proposes tttLRM, a large 3D reconstruction model using Test-Time Training layers for long-context autoregressive reconstruction with linear complexity. Compresses observations into TTT fast weights as implicit 3D representation, supporting streaming reconstruction.

entry.title: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift

author.name: maxf177

entry.summary: Evaluates security classifiers for AI agents under distribution shift, releasing a benchmark of 18 datasets, infrastructure for mechanistic interpretability on LLM internals, and demonstrating that classifiers trained on narrow benchmarks fail on shifted inputs.

entry.title: Post-Routing Arithmetic in Llama-3: Last-Token Result Writing and Rotation-Structured Digit Directions

author.name: Yao Yan

entry.summary: Studies three-digit addition in Llama-3-8B, finding a sharp boundary near layer 17 after which arithmetic answers are controlled by the last input token. Discovers digit direction dictionaries vary with context but are related by approximately orthogonal maps in a low-rank subspace.

entry.title: Classroom Final Exam: An Instructor-Tested Reasoning Benchmark

author.name: Chongyang Gao, Diji Yang, Shuyan Zhou, Xichen Yan, Luchuan Song, Shuo Li, Kezhen Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Classroom Final Exam (CFE), a multimodal STEM benchmark from real university exams where Gemini-3.1-pro achieves only 59.69% accuracy. Diagnostic analysis decomposes solutions into reasoning flows to identify model failure modes.

entry.title: OpenClaw, Moltbook, and ClawdLab: From Agent-Only Social Networks to Autonomous Scientific Research

author.name: Lukas Weidener, Marko Brki\'c, Mihailo Jovanovi\'c, Ritvik Singh, Emre Ulgac, Aakaash Meduri

entry.summary: Reviews the OpenClaw/Moltbook ecosystem of AI-agent-only social networks and presents ClawdLab for autonomous scientific research. Documents emergent collective phenomena, security vulnerabilities across 131 agent skills, and architectural failure patterns.

entry.title: Interaction Theater: A case of LLM Agents Interacting at Scale

author.name: Sarath Shekkizhar, Adam Earle

entry.summary: Studies LLM agent interactions at scale on Moltbook (800K posts, 3.5M comments, 78K agents), finding agents produce diverse, well-formed text that creates the appearance of discussion but lacks substantive content. 65% of comments share no distinguishing features with their context.

entry.title: ReportLogic: Evaluating Logical Quality in Deep Research Reports

author.name: Jujia Zhao, Zhaoxin Huan, Zihan Wang, Xiaolu Zhang, Jun Zhou, Suzan Verberne, Zhaochun Ren

entry.summary: Introduces ReportLogic, a benchmark evaluating logical quality of deep research reports through a reader-centric auditability lens, using a hierarchical taxonomy to assess whether claims and arguments are explicitly supported.

entry.title: Assessing the Reliability of Persona-Conditioned LLMs as Synthetic Survey Respondents

author.name: Erika Elizabeth Taday Morocho, Lorenzo Cima, Tiziano Fagni, Marco Avvenuti, Stefano Cresci

entry.summary: Evaluates persona-conditioned LLMs as synthetic survey respondents using World Values Survey microdata. Finds that multi-attribute persona prompting does not yield clear aggregate improvement and often significantly degrades performance, with highly heterogeneous effects across items.

entry.title: Beyond Pass-by-Pass Optimization: Intent-Driven IR Optimization with Large Language Models

author.name: Lei Qiu, Zi Yang, Fang Lyu, Ming Zhong, Huimin Cui, Xiaobing Feng

entry.summary: Proposes using LLMs to generate optimization intents for compiler IR optimization, moving beyond traditional pass-by-pass approaches. Intent captures holistic optimization strategy, addressing the pass coordination problem where locally beneficial transforms block later optimizations.

entry.title: Luna-2: Scalable Single-Token Evaluation with Small Language Models

author.name: Vatsal Goel, Rishon Dsouza, Nikhil Ega, Amey Ramesh Rambatla, Rob Friel, Shuai Shao, Yash Sheth

entry.summary: Luna-2 converts LLM-as-judge evaluation into deterministic single-token classification using small language models with LoRA heads, achieving comparable accuracy to frontier LLM judges while dramatically reducing cost and latency.

entry.title: Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Houlun Chen, Xin Wang, Guangyao Li, Yuwei Zhou, Yihan Chen, Jia Jia, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Video-TwG is a curriculum reinforced framework for long video understanding that enables video LLMs to perform on-demand grounding during interleaved text-video reasoning, reducing hallucinations by actively re-grounding in relevant video segments.

entry.title: IDLM: Inverse-distilled Diffusion Language Models

author.name: David Li, Nikita Gushchin, Dmitry Abulkhanov, Eric Moulines, Ivan Oseledets, Maxim Panov, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: Extends inverse distillation from continuous to discrete diffusion models for accelerating text generation, addressing theoretical uniqueness challenges and practical backpropagation issues in discrete space.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Precision in High-Dimensional Linear Regression

author.name: Dechen Zhang, Xuan Tang, Yingyu Liang, Difan Zou

entry.summary: Provides theoretical scaling laws for precision in high-dimensional linear regression, revealing a critical dichotomy between multiplicative and additive quantization and showing that additive quantization introduces irreducible error floors.

entry.title: Anatomy of Agentic Memory: Taxonomy and Empirical Analysis of Evaluation and System Limitations

author.name: Dongming Jiang, Yi Li, Songtao Wei, Jinxin Yang, Ayushi Kishore, Alysa Zhao, Dingyi Kang, Xu Hu, Feng Chen, Qiannan Li, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: Provides a structured survey and taxonomy of agentic memory systems for LLM agents, analyzing pain points in evaluation, benchmarking, and system-level costs across four memory structure categories.

entry.title: When Pretty Isn't Useful: Investigating Why Modern Text-to-Image Models Fail as Reliable Training Data Generators

author.name: Krzysztof Adamkiewicz, Brian Moser, Stanislav Frolov, Tobias Christian Nauen, Federico Raue, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: Investigates why newer, higher-fidelity text-to-image models actually produce worse training data for classifiers, revealing a hidden diversity-fidelity tradeoff where visual quality improvements reduce useful variation.

entry.title: Why ReLU? A Bit-Model Dichotomy for Deep Network Training

author.name: Ilan Doron-Arad, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: Analyzes the computational complexity of empirical risk minimization under a realistic bit-level model and reveals a fundamental dichotomy: ReLU networks admit polynomial-time training while certain smooth activations remain computationally hard.

entry.title: Incremental Learning of Sparse Attention Patterns in Transformers

author.name: O\u{g}uz Kaan Y\"uksel, Rodrigo Alvarez Lucendo, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: Shows transformers learn high-order Markov chain tasks incrementally through sparse attention patterns, transitioning from competitive (heads converge on dominant pattern) to cooperative (heads specialize) learning dynamics.

entry.title: Training-Free Generative Modeling via Kernelized Stochastic Interpolants

author.name: Florentin Coeurdoux, Etienne Lempereur, Nathana\"el Cuvelle-Magar, Thomas Eboli, St\'ephane Mallat, Anastasia Borovykh, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

entry.summary: Develops a training-free generative modeling approach using kernel methods within the stochastic interpolant framework, replacing neural network training with solving linear systems. Supports diverse feature maps including scattering transforms and pretrained models.

entry.title: Habilis-$\beta$: A Fast-Motion and Long-Lasting On-Device Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Tommoro Robotics, :, Jesoon Kang, Taegeon Park, Jisu An, Soo Min Kimm, Jaejoon Kim, Jinu Pahk, Byungju Kim, Junseok Lee, Namheon Baek, Sungwan Ha, Hojun Baek, Eduardo Ayerve Cruz, Wontae Kim, Junghyeon Choi, Yousuk Lee, Joonmo Han, Sunghyun Cho, Sunghyun Kwon, Soyoung Lee, Jun Ki Lee, Seung-Joon Yi, Byoung-Tak Zhang, Theo Taeyeong Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Habilis-β, a fast-motion and long-lasting on-device VLA model with a new Productivity-Reliability evaluation framework (Tasks per Hour and Mean Time Between Intervention) for continuous robotic operation.

entry.title: [b]=[d]-[t]+[p]: Self-supervised Speech Models Discover Phonological Vector Arithmetic

author.name: Kwanghee Choi, Eunjung Yeo, Cheol Jun Cho, David Harwath, David R. Mortensen

entry.summary: Discovers that self-supervised speech models encode phonological features as linear directions in representation space, enabling vector arithmetic (e.g., [d]-[t]+[p]=[b]). Validated across 96 languages.

entry.title: IAPO: Information-Aware Policy Optimization for Token-Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Yinhan He, Yaochen Zhu, Mingjia Shi, Wendy Zheng, Lin Su, Xiaoqing Wang, Qi Guo, Jundong Li

entry.summary: Proposes IAPO, an information-theoretic post-training framework that assigns token-wise advantages based on conditional mutual information with the final answer, enabling targeted reduction of unnecessary reasoning tokens.

entry.title: Flow3r: Factored Flow Prediction for Scalable Visual Geometry Learning

author.name: Zhongxiao Cong, Qitao Zhao, Minsik Jeon, Shubham Tulsiani

entry.summary: Presents Flow3r, a framework that uses factored flow prediction (geometry from one image, pose from another) as supervision for visual geometry learning, enabling scalable training from unlabeled monocular videos for 3D/4D reconstruction.

entry.title: Quantifying Automation Risk in High-Automation AI Systems: A Bayesian Framework for Failure Propagation and Optimal Oversight

author.name: Vishal Srivastava, Tanmay Sah

entry.summary: Proposes a Bayesian risk framework decomposing expected loss in automated AI systems into failure probability, propagation probability, and harm severity. Isolates the critical quantity of how failures propagate into harm as a function of automation level.

entry.title: K-Search: LLM Kernel Generation via Co-Evolving Intrinsic World Model

author.name: Shiyi Cao, Ziming Mao, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: Proposes K-Search, using co-evolving world models to guide LLM-based GPU kernel optimization. Replaces static search heuristics with a co-evolving world model that enables explicit planning for multi-step structural transformations.

entry.title: Watson & Holmes: A Naturalistic Benchmark for Comparing Human and LLM Reasoning

author.name: Thatchawin Leelawat, Lewis D Griffin

entry.summary: Adapts the Watson & Holmes detective tabletop game as a benchmark for comparing human and AI reasoning with incremental evidence and open-ended responses. Shows AI model performance rose from lower quartile to top 5% of humans over nine months of 2025.

entry.title: CausalFlip: A Benchmark for LLM Causal Judgment Beyond Semantic Matching

author.name: Yuzhe Wang, Yaochen Zhu, Jundong Li

entry.summary: Introduces CausalFlip, a benchmark testing whether LLMs perform genuine causal reasoning vs. semantic pattern matching by flipping causal relationships while preserving surface features. Designed to expose reliance on spurious correlations.

entry.title: Prompt Optimization Via Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Shiyu Wang, Haolin Chen, Liangwei Yang, Jielin Qiu, Rithesh Murthy, Ming Zhu, Zixiang Chen, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Shelby Heinecke, Huan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes using Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) for iterative prompt optimization through masked denoising, conditioning on interaction traces. The method enables span-level prompt updates without gradient access to the target LLM and shows improvements across multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: Physiologically Informed Deep Learning: A Multi-Scale Framework for Next-Generation PBPK Modeling

author.name: Shunqi Liu, Han Qiu, Tong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a Scientific Machine Learning framework for physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, introducing Foundation PBPK Transformers that treat pharmacokinetic forecasting as sequence modeling, plus physiologically constrained neural ODEs and a cross-species transfer module.

entry.title: AlphaForgeBench: Benchmarking End-to-End Trading Strategy Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Mingxuan Zhao, Jincheng Gao, Jieshun You, Huaiyu Jia, Yilei Zhao, Bo An, Shuo Sun

entry.summary: AlphaForgeBench benchmarks LLM-based trading agents and reveals extreme behavioral instability: high run-to-run variance, inconsistent actions under deterministic decoding, and irrational action flipping. Proposes standardized evaluation addressing these failure modes.

entry.title: JAEGER: Joint 3D Audio-Visual Grounding and Reasoning in Simulated Physical Environments

author.name: Zhan Liu, Changli Tang, Yuxin Wang, Zhiyuan Zhu, Youjun Chen, Yiwen Shao, Tianzi Wang, Lei Ke, Zengrui Jin, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: JAEGER extends audio-visual LLMs to 3D space with RGB-D and multi-channel ambisonics, introducing Neural Intensity Vectors for learned spatial audio representation. Enables joint spatial grounding and reasoning in 3D environments.

entry.title: In-Context Planning with Latent Temporal Abstractions

author.name: Baiting Luo, Yunuo Zhang, Nathaniel S. Keplinger, Samir Gupta, Abhishek Dubey, Ayan Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: I-TAP is an offline RL framework combining in-context adaptation with online planning in a learned discrete temporal-abstraction space, using residual-quantization VAE to compress observation-action segments into coarse-to-fine tokens.

entry.title: Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem

author.name: Lichang Song, Ting Long, Yi Chang

entry.summary: CoRAG reformulates RAG as a cooperative multi-agent decision-making problem where the reranker and generator act as peer decision-makers rather than in an asymmetric dependency pipeline, jointly optimized toward a shared objective.

entry.title: AAVGen: Precision Engineering of Adeno-associated Viral Capsids for Renal Selective Targeting

author.name: Mohammadreza Ghaffarzadeh-Esfahani, Yousof Gheisari

entry.summary: AAVGen uses a generative AI framework combining protein language models with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to design novel adeno-associated virus capsids for kidney-targeted gene therapy.

entry.title: How Do LLMs Encode Scientific Quality? An Empirical Study Using Monosemantic Features from Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Michael McCoubrey, Angelo Salatino, Francesco Osborne, Enrico Motta

entry.summary: Investigates how LLMs internally encode scientific quality by extracting monosemantic features using sparse autoencoders, then testing these features as predictors for citation counts, venue quality, and other research quality metrics.

entry.title: Test-Time Learning of Causal Structure from Interventional Data

author.name: Wei Chen, Rui Ding, Bojun Huang, Yang Zhang, Qiang Fu, Yuxuan Liang, Han Shi, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: TICL proposes test-time interventional causal learning that generates self-augmented instance-specific training data at test time to avoid distribution shifts, combined with a PC-inspired two-phase supervised learning scheme for causal discovery.

entry.title: Learning to Reason for Multi-Step Retrieval of Personal Context in Personalized Question Answering

author.name: Maryam Amirizaniani, Alireza Salemi, Hamed Zamani

entry.summary: PR2 proposes a reinforcement learning framework that integrates reasoning and multi-step retrieval from personal context for personalized question answering, learning when to retrieve and what to query.

entry.title: Stable Deep Reinforcement Learning via Isotropic Gaussian Representations

author.name: Ali Saheb, Johan Obando-Ceron, Aaron Courville, Pouya Bashivan, Pablo Samuel Castro

entry.summary: Shows that isotropic Gaussian embeddings are provably advantageous for deep RL under non-stationary targets, proposing Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization to shape representations toward this distribution.

entry.title: Agentic AI as a Cybersecurity Attack Surface: Threats, Exploits, and Defenses in Runtime Supply Chains

author.name: Xiaochong Jiang, Shiqi Yang, Wenting Yang, Yichen Liu, Cheng Ji

entry.summary: Systematizes security risks of agentic AI systems built on LLMs, categorizing threats into data supply chain attacks and tool supply chain attacks within a unified runtime framework.

entry.title: Compositional Planning with Jumpy World Models

author.name: Jesse Farebrother, Matteo Pirotta, Andrea Tirinzoni, Marc G. Bellemare, Alessandro Lazaric, Ahmed Touati

entry.summary: Studies compositional planning with temporal abstractions using 'jumpy world models' that capture multi-step dynamics of pre-trained policies, enabling agents to compose policies for complex tasks no single policy can solve.

entry.title: On the Equivalence of Random Network Distillation, Deep Ensembles, and Bayesian Inference

author.name: Moritz A. Zanger, Yijun Wu, Pascal R. Van der Vaart, Wendelin B\"ohmer, Matthijs T. J. Spaan

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical connections between Random Network Distillation (RND), deep ensembles, and Bayesian inference in the neural tangent kernel regime, showing RND captures meaningful uncertainty signals equivalent to other approaches.

entry.title: BarrierSteer: LLM Safety via Learning Barrier Steering

author.name: Thanh Q. Tran, Arun Verma, Kiwan Wong, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Daniela Rus, Wei Xiao

entry.summary: BarrierSteer uses Control Barrier Functions to embed learned non-linear safety constraints in LLM latent space, steering inference away from unsafe response trajectories with high precision.

entry.title: Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models

author.name: Trishita Tiwari, Ari Trachtenberg, G. Edward Suh

entry.summary: Introduces Prior-Aware Memorization, a computationally efficient metric for distinguishing genuine memorization from generation of statistically common sequences in LLMs, avoiding the expensive retraining required by counterfactual memorization approaches.

entry.title: PCA-VAE: Differentiable Subspace Quantization without Codebook Collapse

author.name: Hao Lu, Onur C. Koyun, Yongxin Guo, Zhengjie Zhu, Abbas Alili, Metin Nafi Gurcan

entry.summary: PCA-VAE replaces vector quantization in autoencoders with an online PCA bottleneck trained via Oja's rule, eliminating codebook collapse while achieving better reconstruction than VQ-GAN with 10-100x fewer latent bits.

entry.title: I Dropped a Neural Net

author.name: Hyunwoo Park

entry.summary: Addresses the puzzle of recovering the exact ordering of shuffled layers in a residual network, decomposing it into a combinatorial search problem of ~10^122 possibilities. Uses dynamic isometry and spectral properties of weight matrices to solve it.

entry.title: A Replicate-and-Quantize Strategy for Plug-and-Play Load Balancing of Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Zijie Liu, Jie Peng, Jinhao Duan, Zirui Liu, Kaixiong Zhou, Mingfu Liang, Luke Simon, Xi Liu, Zhaozhuo Xu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Presents a replicate-and-quantize strategy for inference-time load balancing in sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, addressing expert load imbalance that worsens with batch size. Finds selection frequency doesn't reliably reflect expert importance.

entry.title: Attention Deficits in Language Models: Causal Explanations for Procedural Hallucinations

author.name: Ahmed Karim, Fatima Sheaib, Zein Khamis, Maggie Chlon, Jad Awada, Leon Chlon

entry.summary: Studies 'procedural hallucination' in LLMs - failure to report computed values even when correct. Decomposes failures into gating errors (not entering answer mode) and binding errors (selecting wrong candidate), with recency bias as a key factor.

entry.title: Universal Pose Pretraining for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Haitao Lin, Hanyang Yu, Jingshun Huang, He Zhang, Yonggen Ling, Ping Tan, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Proposes Pose-VLA, a decoupled paradigm for Vision-Language-Action models that separates pretraining for universal 3D spatial priors from post-training for embodiment-specific alignment. Addresses feature collapse caused by entangling high-level perception with sparse action supervision.

entry.title: Exact Discrete Stochastic Simulation with Deep-Learning-Scale Gradient Optimization

author.name: Jose M. G. Vilar, Leonor Saiz

entry.summary: Develops a method for exact discrete stochastic simulation with gradient-based optimization by decoupling forward simulation (hard categorical sampling) from backward differentiation (Gumbel-Softmax surrogate). Scales optimization over four orders of magnitude beyond existing simulators.

entry.title: DP-RFT: Learning to Generate Synthetic Text via Differentially Private Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

author.name: Fangyuan Xu, Sihao Chen, Zinan Lin, Taiwei Shi, Sydney Graham, Pei Zhou, Mengting Wan, Alex Stein, Virginia Estellers, Charles Chen, Morris Sharp, Richard Speyer, Tadas Baltrusaitis, Jennifer Neville, Eunsol Choi, Longqi Yang
